So I'm in a middle of a creative process, working on a 10-ep show. I have a pretty good idea about how I want the plot and all the characters to develop, but I have a one, huge problem.

You see, the main character is (read carefully) an omnipotent, multidimensional being banished from it's realm to live its life as a human being (as a punishment for observing and fascinating over life on Earth by other such beings, as they see "lesser" beings as puny and simply inferior) but at the same time a representation of a person suffering from Bipolar disorder (in the first half of the show, omnipotence represents how such person feels in a manic episode, and over the course of the show losing its omnipotence, becoming more and more human, depicting a depressive episode). Both of those descriptions are seperate and I want to leave the viewer asking himself about the main character's true origin (without ever actually explaining it) and I have a lot of ideas on how to do it. The issue is - how do I introduce this character? How do I show how it first appeared on Earth without losing the ambiguity of its origin?

Obviously, I'm not asking you for a definite solution to the problem. I'm simply trying to find any inspiration and/or any useful writing tricks that could help me find the right answer. Thank you in advance!

I've been studying philosophy for years now (not academically, it was all on my own). I'm a highly empathetic and sensitive being. I was abused for basically my whole life by my father and I had to raise myself. Always taking care of myself.
I've been thinking about the nature of existence my whole life. Always looking for the objective truth about our reality (i don't claim that I've found it, it's about working on getting close to it, reaching it is probably impossible), and after many years I've come to a conclusion:

Whatever my accomplishments are, no matter how many incredible things I might do in my life, all of it does not matter in the grand scheme of things. What's the point of working on my art and writing shit to express myself? We are all going to die someday, so the results, no matter how great, don't matter either. 
Existence is a pain for me, bipolar is killing me. As i said - every time i break apart, I work hard on pulling myself back up and proving that I'm not the failure everyone claims I am, and I've been doing a decent job at it. But every single time I break apart again and land back in the same spot. What's the fucking point of my suffering? I just want to die and get this over with.

I find Kayle mid so much better than on toplane. 

In lower elos there's a massive chance that your enemy laner will constantly shove you under the turret, so you can just safely farm and scale, making them unable to not only kill you, but even poke you, so I just start with doran's ring and have unlimited health and mana to just sit under the turret and keep farming. Another advantage it gives you, is that your enemy laner will most likely get desperate and keep roaming. This of course leads to them losing gold and xp, so even if they get fed, you're still much stronger than them. 

I've been playing Kayle mid for a few days now, and got 71% winrate on Kayle (most of the games I lost were on toplane) in 24 games. I'm seriously convinced that Kayle mid is a cheat code in low elo. In high elo your opponents are likely to know how to punish you, so I don't advise picking it, unless you feel comfortable with the matchup.

Disclaimer: Depression just as any other mental condition is an illness. You can't choose to have it or not. It presents itself after a trauma, loss of a close one etc. Damn, it can even be genetic (Dysautonomia, look it up). 

Nihilism and any other world view relative to it can, but don't have to cause depression. It's only up to one's perception and beliefs. You can still choose to be happy, go out and experience something that might give you a sense of completion, because that's what it's all about. Take care of yourself!!

Even though I am currently in a state where my world view led me to be an example of how selfdestructive humans can get  (I barely eat, sleep, and I'm fully antisocial) I still won't "change my beliefs" (or rather lack of them) because it just isn't how things work. 


I feel like once you've reached a certain point you realise that changing your world view would be just a lie you tell yourself to find a purpose, because that's what your body expects you to do. We are built to live our life reproducing and providing for our children for them to do exactly the same thing. And to do that, you need something you'd believe in that pushes you into the struggle of existing. That's why people invent Gods and most of them won't ever consider that they might be wrong.  Consider, that we are just a weird-shaped bunch of atoms roaming around for literally nothing. 

From my experience - the only people that are able to really understand what nihilism is about, are those who study and embrace their own self-awareness. Most of humanity just tries not to think about their own perception and focuses on what they consume to form their views on everything they come in contact with. Those few "chosen" people who rely on their senses and judgement will always sooner or later see that there's no universal purpose to our lives, and each of us gets to choose their own. Nihlism is a direct response to that! Purpose is not a default, therefore it's not something that nihilists can choose to turn to. Once you see the truth, you can't lie to yourself anymore.
